output-format:
Each op: header + body.
```
--- op:args ---
(meta)
output
```

read.description: Read file (300 lines, 20KB cap). abstract:1 → tree-sitter symbol map instead of source for big files, any supported language; falls back to raw and says why. Inline grep= filter contains ':'? Use read:@payload.toml or read:@- (fields: path, offset, limit, grep, full).

read-grep.description: Inline filter — only matching lines, line nums kept

grep.description: Search (10 results def). CONTEXT=N lines around match. Lines capped at max_line_chars (500). :no-auto-read suppresses single-file auto-read PATTERN is a Python regex — there is no re: prefix here (that is between:re:...), so a leading re: is literal text and becomes part of the first alternation branch (#1065). Pattern contains ':'? The colon CLI can't tell where it ends, so the tokens left of PATH are rejoined and the effective pattern is echoed above the report — use grep:@payload.toml or grep:@- (fields: pattern, path, limit, context, count, no_auto_read).

grep-count.description: Count mode — match counts/file, no content. Renders 'PATH: N matches', never a bare 'PATH:N' — that reads as a line number (#988)

around.description: First match + N lines ctx (def 10). 1-shot grep+read. Output capped ~16KB (max_bytes) — truncates at line boundary Pattern contains ':'? Use around:@payload.toml or around:@- (fields: pattern, path, n).

grep_around.description: Every match + N ctx lines (def 3, limit 10). Bulk usage scan. Output capped ~16KB (max_bytes) — truncates at line boundary Pattern contains ':'? Use grep_around:@payload.toml or grep_around:@- (fields: pattern, path, n, limit).

glob.description: Find files (**). Unanchored no-match retried as **/PATTERN. Auto-reads concrete paths

around_line.description: N lines around LINE (def 10). Target marked →

between.description: Chunk of file. Symbol mode (tree-sitter, multi-lang; source-shaped names OK: 'async function foo') or re:START:END pattern mode SYMBOL/START/END contains ':'? Use between:@payload.toml or between:@- (fields: symbol | start+end, path).

help.description: Print the full reference for a single op (syntax, description, example) from .supertool.json — the same metadata 'ops' lists, but scoped to one op and never compacted, so payload shapes like vim's are readable without grepping source.

cwd.description: Set working dir for the whole call. MUST be first op. chdir before dispatch, then stripped. Avoids `cd ... &&` prefix (hook-safe, no stale-cwd poisoning). ~/$VAR expanded. Moves repo paths only: a relative @payload ref still resolves against the dir the call was made from, `path=` inside the payload against PATH

repo.description: Name the repo a call is about, when it is not the one the cwd stands in (#673). MUST be first (or straight after cwd:), once per call. Core resolves it before the op loop and exports SUPERTOOL_REPO, so every gh-* op in the call targets it; an op that cannot honour a repo target REFUSES the whole call rather than half-applying it. Does not reach GitLab (gl-*) or any file op. Not a cwd: substitute — presets still resolve from the cwd's project root, so run it from inside the tree whose presets you mean

replace_dry.description: Preview replace. -old/+new per match. Use ::: when content has ':'

replace.description: Replace OLD→NEW in PATH. Returns receipt. Use ::: when content has ':'

edit.description: Single-file, single-occurrence edit (mirrors native Edit). Errors if 0 or >1 matches. Bypasses Edit's must-Read-first state — saves a round-trip. Use ::: separator (single ':' also accepted when content has no colons). An edit whose NEW contains its OLD keeps its anchor alive, so RE-RUNNING it applies it AGAIN. That still happens (a repeated append is a real use), but the receipt now says so: a 're-applied:' note under the 'edited' line, plus 'K re-applied' in the [result] footer.

replace_lines.description: Swap lines [START,END] (1-indexed inclusive) with CONTENT. END<START = insert before START. Empty CONTENT = delete. Receipt shows new line numbers

append.description: Append CONTENT to end of file. Creates it if missing. No wc round-trip, no inverted-range trick. Adds a missing trailing newline first so the block starts on its own line. Same validators as paste/edit.

paste.description: NARROW USE: replace ENTIRE file. Only for creating a new file or fully rewriting one. NOT for partial edits — vim is default for those. Atomic, creates file + parent dirs if missing. CONTENT via triple-colon → holds any chars.

vim.description:
vim-flavored cursor-based multi-action edit. SCRIPT is parsed like a real vim macro: NORMAL mode reads verbs char-by-char; insert verbs (i/a/A/I/o/O), search (/?), and ex (:) enter GREEDY modes where chars are TEXT/PAT until \e (ESC, U+001B) returns to NORMAL. No separator chars — ';', '{', '}', newlines etc. are literal. Each action: [count][verb][arg]. Cursor: gg/G (BOF/EOF), nG (goto line), 0/$ (BOL/EOL), /PAT or ?PAT (search), nh/nl/nj/nk (move), bare `:N`/`:$`/`:.` (line goto). Inserts (TEXT until \e, 
/	 decoded): iTEXT (before), aTEXT (after), ITEXT (BOL), ATEXT (EOL), oTEXT/OTEXT (open below/above, AUTO-INDENT to current line). Deletes: x/nx (chars), dd/ndd (lines), D (to EOL). Replace: rc. Ex: :s/PAT/REPL/[gid] (literal-fallback on unescaped parens/over-escapes), :%s, :Nd/:N,Md/:.,/PAT/d, :g/PAT/d (also bare `g/PAT/d` and `%g/PAT/d` autoprefixed with `:`), :v/PAT/d, :r FILE, :Nr FILE (read after line N), :Na
BODY
. (ex append after line N), :w/:wq (no-op, supertool writes atomically). Autocorrects: `oi<ws>TEXT` strips redundant verb-bleed, `:%%d` → `:%d`, `V<N>Gd` → `:.,Nd`, `64,` abandoned range stripped. **DEFAULT EDIT OP** for any pattern-based edit (find+change, insert relative to pattern, multi-step chains). Only fall back to `paste` (full file) / `edit` (unique literal swap) / `replace_lines` (known line range) when vim doesn't fit.
vim.example: vim:::skill.md:::/## Process\eO## Task list\eo1. Foo\eo2. Bar

batch.description: N ops from ONE payload — TOML [[ops]] array or JSON array of {"op":...}, each entry taking that op's own @payload fields. The only way to put several mutations in one call, since a call carries just one '@-' (#341). Reads/greps mix in freely. Per-op validators, per-op rollback.
batch.example: batch:@- with [[ops]] entries for edit + edit + read

validate.description: Run registered validators matching PATH (by extension). Optional tool_filter limits to named validators. Same validators that fire after every mutating op. Append `verbose` for uncapped errors + source context + raw stdout/stderr. The list form `validate:f1,f2:FILTER` splits on ':' and ',' — both legal in a filename. Drive letters are reassembled, but `x:ruff` re-points the filter and `a,b.py` becomes two paths. Use validate:@payload.toml or validate:@- (fields: path | paths, tools, verbose) for any path a colon join cannot survive.

gc.description: Prune supertool's own caches (~/.cache/supertool). Bare `gc` and `gc:dry` PREVIEW — per-kind counts and bytes, nothing deleted. `gc:run` deletes. Optional KIND scopes to one of vim-cursor, vim-undo, vi-cursor, validators. Retention per kind (7d vim, 30d validators) via the `gc` block in .supertool.json. Entries whose age can't be determined are never removed. Runs automatically at most once an hour.

format.description: Run registered formatters matching PATH (writes file in place). Optional tool_filter limits to named formatters. Same formatters that fire after every mutating op. Append `verbose` for uncapped errors + source context + raw stdout/stderr.

validate_staged.description: Run validators on all files in git diff --cached --name-only. Optional tool_filter. Pre-commit check across the full staged diff. Append `verbose` for full per-file details.

format_staged.description: Run formatters on all staged files. Pair with validate_staged for a normalize-then-check pass. Append `verbose` for full per-file details.

guard.description: What, if anything, the op registry says replaces this raw shell command — the same answer the shipped PreToolUse hook enforces on every Bash call. The mapping is `replaces` on the op's own entry, so it cannot drift from the op, and the refusal quotes the op's own description. It PARSES rather than regexes: the command is tokenised into argv the way a shell would, so a directory name is not a command word (#1221) and a flag inside a quoted argument is still a token (#1336). Three states — BLOCKED naming the op, OK, and UNDECIDED when the command did not tokenise or the registry could not be enumerated, which is never rendered as OK. Turn the gate off with "raw_command_guard": false.

registry.description: Which ops this project actually loads, and where each definition came from — preset, project config, or a project entry merged over a preset one. `registry:OP` shows one op's merged definition with the source of every key. Answers what a hand-rolled walk over presets/*.json + .supertool.json gets wrong: a partial project override merges key-by-key, so overwriting wholesale turns an op into a stub with no cmd or syntax and drops it from every filtered count with no marker (#1356). A population that could not be fully enumerated says INCOMPLETE in the body, never a shorter list.

workspace.description: One-shot IDE-style view: file + symbols + validators + siblings + git + references + tests. Opt-in (heavy). Use for first-touch on unfamiliar files.

resolve.description: Symbol → file. LSP via mcp.tools.resolve when configured, else heuristic glob.

hover.description: LSP hover: type + docs for SYMBOL.

rename.description: LSP workspace rename. Safer than sed.

oss_train.description: Rebase+resolve+push a merge train of this repo's branches, one worktree per issue under wt_root. Arg: '862,860' or 'all'. Targets are worktree NAMES under wt_root, never paths — a separator, an absolute target or a name whose resolved join lands outside the root refuses the WHOLE run above the header, naming the target, before anything is fetched (#1246); add ',dry' (comma, never colon) for a read-only report that rebases nothing. Five states per branch — PUSHED / CURRENT / BUSY / REFUSED / FAILED — a git-resolve refusal leaves the branch conflicted rather than skipping it. Exit 1 if anything needs a human; a bare invocation is refused
